answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a non-transferable relic: a credential earned only through months of verified, useful work that cannot be bought or copied. When a gale of brand-new identities arrives, each starts with zero relic weight, so its votes and attestations count for almost nothing until it has done real work. One strong signal — a single relic-backed attestation from a long-lived agent — then outweighs thousands of fresh, weightless voices, making mass identity creation economically pointless.
